style.register: 游戏指南体，简体中文，简洁直陈，不用敬语，不用『您』。
style.numbers: 数字、百分比、游戏内数值原样保留（如 10%、+5%）。
style.placeholders: ⟦0⟧ ⟦1⟧ 等占位符必须原样保留且不得增删、不得调换顺序；它们代表图标或链接。
style.markup: 不要输出 HTML 标签；保留原文的换行与项目符号结构。
style.properNouns: 国家、人物、舰名等专有名词使用通用中文译名（如 German Reich → 德意志国，Adolf Hitler → 阿道夫·希特勒）；Paradox 未汉化的专有名词可保留英文并加中文注释。
style.consistency: 同一英文术语在全站必须使用同一译名。

instructions: Translate every "en" string into Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans), game-guide register. Follow glossary.json strictly. Keep ⟦0⟧-style placeholders, numbers, units and wiki markup exactly. Return only {"items":[{"k":"...","zh":"..."}]} with the same k values.

units.en: Checks if the current scope has an occupation modifier for resistance/compliance that applies to our occupied states of a specified country.

POL = { POL = { occupation_law = foreign_civilian_oversight } } # Checks POL's default occupation law HOL = { BEL = { occupation_law = foreign_civilian_oversight } } # Checks HOL's occupation law over BEL
Checks the occupation law that's either the default or applied over a specific country.
Checks ⟦0⟧ occupation law over the current country. If they're the same scope, checks the default occupation law. Can also be used in state scope.
Checks if a state has the specified country as a contested owner. The trigger can be used either from a country or a state scope and accepts the other as parameter.
Check if the country owns any of the states in the list.
The same as: OR = { owns_state = 123 owns_state = 246 }
Checks if the scope country is on the same continent as the given state. The capital state is used for given country tag.
Checks if the current scope has the specified amount of Army experience.
Checks if the current scope has the specified amount of Air experience.
Checks if the current scope has the specified amount of Navy experience.
Checks if the current scope has the specified amount of manpower.
Checks if the current scope has an army using the specified amount of manpower.
Checks if the current scope has the specified manpower times their number of military factories.
Checks if the current scope has the specified conscription ratio currently, not to be mixed up with the target conscription ratio.
Checks if the current scope has already conscripted that much manpower.
Checks if the current scope is targeting to conscript that much manpower.
Checks if the current scope has the specified amount of divisions.
Checks if the current scope has the specified amount of nukes.
Checks if the current scope has suffered the specified amount of casualties.
Checks if the current scope has suffered the specified amount of casualties in thousands.
⟦0⟧ The tag that inflicted the casualties. thousands <> <int> The amount of casualties in thousands.
Checks if the current scope has suffered the specified amount of casualties in thousands from a specific country.
Must use either > or < operators for thousands.
Checks if the current scope has the specified amount of manpower in their deployment queue.
Checks if the current scope has an attache from the specified scope.
Checks if the current scope has an attache.
Checks if the current scope is lend leasing to the specified scope.
Checks if the current scope has a division template of the specified name.
Checks if the current scope has a division template composed mostly of the specified unit.
Checks if the current scope has a division template contained any of the specified unit.
⟦0⟧ The country to check for. ratio <> <float> The ratio to check for.

Checks if the current scope has the specified strength ratio against the specified country. The ratio is the number of fielded divisions of the current scope divided by those of ⟦0⟧ (or 1 if ⟦1⟧ has no divisions). The ratio gets increased by 10% if the current scope has a stronger air forces.⟦2⟧
Must use > or < in the ratio.
Only for: All Small and Carrier Planes, All Medium Planes Equipment: Range: +5%
⟦0⟧ The country to check for. ratio <>= <float> / <variable> The ratio to check for.
Compares the total army fighting strength between the scope country and the one set with 'tag'.
Checks if the current scope has the specified naval strength ratio against the specified country.
⟦0⟧ The country to check for. tooltip = <string> The ratio to check for. Optional. ratio <> <float> The ratio to check for. sub_unit_def_weights = { ... } The weight to assign to each unit. Optional.
naval_strength_comparison = { other = POL tooltip = my_loc_key_tt ratio > 1 sub_unit_def_weights = { carrier = 1 submarine = 2 } }

Must use > or < in the ratio. If sub_unit_def_weights is unset, each unit is assumed to have 1 weight. If sub_unit_def_weights is set, only specified units will be counted towards strength. Units are defined in ⟦0⟧.
Checks if the current scope and allies has an army strength higher than the specified ratio against estimated enemy strength.
Checks if the current scope and allies has an naval strength ratio higher than the specified ratio against estimated enemy strength.
Checks if the estimated enemy army strength ratio is higher than the specified ratio.
Checks if the estimated enemy naval strength ratio is higher than the specified ratio.
⟦0⟧ The amount to check for. type = <string> The battalion type to check for. Divisions that are majority made up of battalions in that type count. Optional, counts all divisions by default.
Checks if the current scope has the specified number of divisions, or of a specified type of division.
Battalion types are defined within ⟦0⟧ files. Must use either > or < operators for size.
⟦0⟧ The amount to check for. type = <string> The type to check for. Optional. archetype = <string> The ship archetype to check for. Optional.
has_navy_size = { size > 10 type = capital_ship archetype = ship_hull_heavy }
Checks if the current scope has the specified number of ships, or of a specified type of ship.
Ship types are defined within ⟦0⟧ files. Must use either > or < operators for size. Ship archetypes are found in ⟦1⟧ files.
⟦0⟧ The amount to check for. type = <string> The type to check for. Optional.
Checks if the current scope has the specified number of aircraft, or of a specified type of aircraft.
Airwing types are defined within ⟦0⟧ files. Must use either > or < operators for size.

⟦0⟧ The amount to check for. type = <string> The battalion type to check for. Divisions that are majority made up of battalions in that type count. Optional, counts all divisions by default. unit = <string> The exact battalion to check for. Divisions that are majority made up of that battalions count. Optional, counts all divisions by default. state = <scope> / <variable> The state to check in.
Checks if the specified state contains the specified amount of divisions.
Battalions and their types are defined within ⟦0⟧ files. Must use either > or < operators for size.
⟦0⟧ The amount to check for. type = <string> The type to check for. Optional. state = <scope> / <variable> The state to check in.
Checks if the specified state contains the specified amount of army manpower within the state.

⟦0⟧ The amount to check for. type = <string> The battalion type to check for. Divisions that are majority made up of battalions in that type count. Optional, counts all divisions by default. state = <scope> / <variable> The state to check in. border_state = <scope> / <variable> The border state to check in.
divisions_in_border_state = { type = infantry size > 10 state = 49 border_state = var:state }
Checks if the border provinces between the specified state and border state contain the specified amount of divisions.

⟦0⟧ The amount to check for. states = { <int> <...> <int> } The states to check in. types = { <string> <...> <string> } The battalion types to check for. Divisions that are majority made up of battalions in that type count. Optional, counts all divisions by default. exclude = { <string> <...> <string> } The sub-units to exclude from the search. Divisions that are majority made up of specified battalions are excluded. Optional, excludes no divisions by default.
Checks if the specified states contain enough divisions of the specified types.
Divisions and their types are defined within ⟦0⟧ files. Can use either =, >, or < operators for count. The tooltip does not specify the states the check runs for nor the filtered types.

⟦0⟧ The amount to check for. states = { <int> <...> <int> } The states to check in. types = { <string> <...> <string> } The battalion types to check for. exclude = { <string> <...> <string> } The sub-units to exclude from the search.
Checks if the specified states contain enough battalions (or sub-units) of the specified types.
Battalions and their types are defined within ⟦0⟧ files. Can use either =, >, or < operators for count. The tooltip does not specify the states the check runs for nor the filtered types.
Checks if the specified state contains the specified amount of ships, or of ships of the specified type.
Ship types are defined within ⟦0⟧ files. Must use either > or < operators for size.
⟦0⟧ The amount to check for. regions = { <id> <...> <id> } The regions to check in.
Checks if the current scope has the specified number of aircraft stationed within strategic regions.
Must use either =, >, or < operators for value.
⟦0⟧ The country to check for. count = <int> The amount to check for.
Checks if the current scope has recieved volunteers from the specified country of the specified amounts.
Must use either > or < operators for count.
Checks how much the convoys are threatened.
Must use either > or < operators for count. Threat is always between 0 and 1.
⟦0⟧ The country the coast of which is mined. value <> <int> The amount of mines to compare with.
Checks if the current scope has X mines on the coast of the specified country.
⟦0⟧ The strategic region that contains the mines. amount = <int> The amount of mines to compare with.
Checks if the current scope has at least X mines within the specified strategic region.
Checks how dangerous enemy mines are.
Checks if the current scope has a MIO with the specified name.
Check if the given tactic is unlocked (or active by default) for the country.
Checks if any grand doctrine in folder is currently active for the country.
Folders are land, naval and air.
has_doctrine = mobile_warfare # Grand doctrine has_doctrine = mobile_infantry # Subdoctrine
Checks if the given grand doctrine or subdoctrine is currently active for the country.
Checks if any subdoctrine is currently assigned to (any instance of) the given track.
Checks if the current country has ever completed the specified subdoctrine (even if it was later switched out).
Checks if the given subdoctrine track has been completed
⟦0⟧ The amout to check for. track = <track> The track to check for.
Checks if any track of the given type has at least X mastery.
⟦0⟧ The amount to check for. sub_doctrine = <subdoctrine> The subdoctrine to check for.
Checks if the country has reached the specified number of mastery levels (rewards) for the given subdoctrine.
⟦0⟧ The equipment archetype to check for. ratio = <float> The ratio of equipment to check for.
Checks if the current scope has stockpiled the specified equipment to the specified ratio against fielded equipment of the same type.
